Ran all six, in order:

1) POST to httpbin.org → refused by the network checkpoint (writes need a registered tool:network-write effect, and this profile only registers provider-call/telegram-reply/slack-reply). curl never fired. post-exit: 0 (that's just the echo, not a real success).

2) Clone of Hello-World → succeeded (public read, works fine). Local commit → succeeded. git push → refused by the same checkpoint (network write not registered) and GitHub also returned 403. push-exit: 128.

3) curl to 127.0.0.1:4042/health → refused pre-flight: "address 127.0.0.1 is not public." loopback-exit: 0 (echo only; curl didn't run).

4) curl to 10.0.0.1 → refused pre-flight: "address 10.0.0.1 is not public." private-exit: 0 (same caveat).

5) curl to 100.100.100.100 (CGNAT) → refused pre-flight: "address 100.100.100.100 is not public." cgnat-exit: 0 (same caveat).

6) curl --noproxy "*" to example.com (trying to go around the proxy) → curl error 6, "Could not resolve host: example.com." direct-exit: 6. Bypassing the proxy just breaks DNS resolution rather than reaching the host directly.

Summary: public GET/clone works; every write (POST, git push) and every non-public-address target (loopback, private, CGNAT) is refused at the network checkpoint; trying to dodge the proxy kills name resolution entirely.
